hotspots.title: Vox’s constitutional crusade against Spain’s PM over Ceuta
hotspots.blurb: Vox escalates legal threats against Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, demanding his prosecution under Article 102 of Spain’s Constitution for alleged treason and state security crimes over the Ceuta migration crisis. The party frames this as a moral and legal imperative to defend Spain’s sovereignty.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high-stakes legal framing, moral panic over migration, and the potential to reshape Spain’s political landscape ahead of elections.

hotspots.title: Javier Milei’s Messi tribute sparks outrage
hotspots.blurb: Argentine President Javier Milei’s effusive praise for Lionel Messi after his father’s death, calling him 'the greatest human in Argentina’s history,' ignited backlash. Critics accuse Milei of politicizing grief and exploiting Messi’s global stature for personal gain.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to the emotional resonance of Messi’s legacy, the perceived insensitivity of Milei’s timing, and the broader cultural divide it exposes in Argentina.

hotspots.title: AfD’s surge in German state elections
hotspots.blurb: Germany’s far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) leads polls in Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-West Pomerania, and Berlin, with potential to govern alone in one state. The party’s rise triggers fears of democratic backsliding and EU instability.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to the existential threat it poses to Germany’s political consensus, the alarmist framing of its extremist ties, and the cross-party panic over its electoral momentum.

hotspots.title: Nigel Farage’s firebombing probe reignites
hotspots.blurb: Counter-terrorism police reopened the investigation into a 2025 firebombing attempt at Nigel Farage’s London home, initially dismissed as a burglary. The probe’s revival amid Farage’s political resurgence fuels speculation about targeted attacks on right-wing figures.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to the violent imagery, the victim’s high-profile status, and the conspiracy theories it fuels about political persecution.

hotspots.title: Tisza Party’s presidential pick sparks constitutional crisis
hotspots.blurb: Hungary’s ruling Tisza Party nominated former Supreme Court chief András Baka as president, defying opposition accusations of illegitimacy. The move escalates tensions over judicial independence and the erosion of democratic norms under Viktor Orbán’s legacy.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to the perceived power grab, the symbolic weight of the presidency, and the cross-party outrage over the nomination’s procedural irregularities.
